mentl/8d5638e:
A closure that performs effects must carry the evidence for them — the per-closure
mirror of a handler arm's captured_evs (handler IS state IS closure IS evidence,
one record, four roles). Lambda + let-bound-fn lowering stubbed the ev_slots to an
empty list, so when the closure was called elsewhere (a higher-order fn's arm
calling `f(x)`) a perform inside it read a bad evidence slot -> out-of-bounds.

Fix: the closure captures $derive_ev_slots(handle) — the evidence for the effects
ITS body performs, read from its own row and resolved at the DEFINITION site (where
those effects' handlers are in scope), exactly as the inline-perform path resolves.
Both layers, both closure paths:
- src/lower.mn LambdaExpr (inline) + the let-bound LLet(.., LMakeClosure) site.
- bootstrap/src/lower/walk_compound.wat (inline lambda) + walk_stmt.wat (let-bound).

The <| / >< parallelism-thunk closures (lower.mn:1244/1282) are a peer: a thunk's
evidence is its BRANCH's row, not its own handle — a distinct shape; the wheel's
hot path (map/for_each/fold via LambdaExpr) is covered.

Verified census-neutral (190 = baseline), micros green (ev2/ev4/ev8=57 ev5=21
ev16=18). Pass-2 advances: the lower_state_init lambda's lookup_ty trap is GONE;
the trap is now a DEEPER link — build_handler_arm_names' map-lambda performing
env_lookup through lower_effect_name_of_op (the evidence threads one call deeper
before the next gap). Each closure now self-carries its evidence.

mentl/8d3d2f7:
Closes the empirically-discovered gap: lambda bodies inside fn
bodies (e.g., `fn main() = (x) => x`) lower to LMakeClosure but
their fn body wasn't emitted at module level. Closure records
referenced $N_idx but no $N function was defined.

Refactors $emit_functions to call a recursive helper
$emit_functions_walk that descends into all common LowExpr
containers — LLet, LBlock, LIf, LCall, LTailCall, LBinOp,
LMakeVariant, LMakeList, LMakeTuple, LReturn, LMakeClosure,
LMakeContinuation. When LMakeClosure or LMakeContinuation is
encountered ANYWHERE in the LowExpr forest (not just at top
level), $emit_fn_body is called for its LowFn AND the helper
recurses into the fn body to find further nested closures.

Eight interrogations cleared per recursion site. Drift modes
refused: Drift 1 (no vtable), Drift 6 (nullary AND N-ary lambdas
share emit path), Drift 9 (all common containers walked
explicitly; non-recursing tags are drift-9-safe because lower
doesn't produce LMakeClosure as direct children of those forms
today).

Empirical verification — `fn main() = (x) => x`:
- Before: only $main and $_start in output; lambda referenced
  $5_idx but no $5 function defined; module would fail wasm-validate
- After: $main + $5 + $_start all emitted; $5 has param $x; the
  lambda body is a real top-level fn

Same applies to closures with captures, tuple-form lambdas (a, b)
=> a + b, and any nested closure pattern.

Per CLAUDE.md ⊕ session-continuity: each commit closes one
substrate gap; the medium folds into its seed continuously.

two-top/8d148c1:
New input_desktop crate maps the keyboard to wire-format PlayerInput
(level signals only): WASD/Space/LShift drive P0, arrows/RShift/RCtrl
drive P1, so two friends play couch versus on one keyboard with no
controllers. Pure input_from_dpad mapping is unit-tested (6 cases);
a thin ReadInputs system emits DISTINCT per-handle LocalInputs.

App wiring: InputTouchPlugin now provides touch/window state on all
platforms, but the ReadInputs source is platform-gated — android keeps
touch, desktop uses the keyboard source (never both: they'd race over
LocalInputs). Local SyncTest input delay dropped 2->0 for snappy couch
feel (a real versus that also self-verifies determinism every frame).
Boots clean; gamepad + a non-SyncTest local session are P.1/P.2 follow-ups.
celezdial/8d8d424:
The app played a birth chart but never said what you were hearing.
Add a "what am i hearing" panel below the keyboard: five short
paragraphs that walk a newcomer from "the twelve signs are the twelve
notes" through degree-tuning, aspects, and orbit, closing on a
one-line system spec (tropical, whole-sign, traditional rulers, 100
cents per sign, Cousto x0.5) for readers who already know the vocabulary.

Every key now carries a hover title with its fixed identity (note,
octave, ruling planet, oscillator, Cousto cents) and any chart
placements at exact degrees. The info panel shows real positions in
astrologer notation, 10 degrees 18 arcminutes, and marks retrograde
bodies with the retrograde glyph (astro.js now reads isRetrograde off
each body). The aspect legend gains color and plain verbs: a
conjunction stacks a voice, trines and sextiles lift theirs, squares
and oppositions set the pair beating. The context line adapts to one
chart or two instead of only describing the dual case.
stoop/8d7567d:
The marker voice was Anton turned a few degrees, which read as a headline
that had been knocked. It is set in Knewave now, a fat felt-tip under the
Open Font License, on screen and on paper: the PDF embeds it as a second
face beside Anton, with its own widths and baseline, and a line breaks on
paper where it broke on screen. Both faces ship as WOFF, the same TrueType
with each table compressed, and the PDF writer unpacks them back to
TrueType before embedding; test/10-typeface checks every table of both
against the files in src/fonts. The build now drops the stylesheet's
comments as it already dropped the script's, and the press stays under
its ratchet with both faces aboard.

A scrap or a piece can go in unsigned. The bell can be added to anybody's
calendar as a file with a reminder the day before. The shelf says when
this browser was last backed up and offers to do it, since until then it
is the only copy, and the press asks the browser to keep its storage once
an issue has shipped. A photograph can say what is in it: screen readers
get it, and the text view prints it under the photograph.
